rows.claim: D-030: a device crash takes the `should_close` path.
rows.evidence: rg finds no `should_close` in src/ or test/. A crash is caught by the wrapper and shares the voluntary-return exit path, `shutdown!` then the `should_abort` consult (src/devices.jl:650-672). D-373 (log.md:15779) dissolved `should_close`. The entry's own annotation at log.md:1170 records the move.
rows.fix: device crash = the wrapper's catch, the same exit path as a voluntary return, with a sim stop only under `should_abort`
rows.note: Stage M lead (names missing: should_close). Moved by D-373. The annotation after Spec already says so, so the Position text needs no edit.

rows.claim: D-059: runtime failures are caught at one site, around the boundary macro-sequence.
rows.evidence: The model has four catch sites, each calling the one constructor `_wrap_step`. They are `frame!` around the whole frame, drain included, as host :loop (src/frame.jl:87-97), boundary zero under `init!` (src/model.jl:335-339), `overlay!`'s settling (src/model.jl:475-479) and the restore door (src/model.jl:1336-1341). See src/model.jl:1069-1076.
rows.fix: Runtime failures are caught at the model's catch sites (`frame!` around the frame, and each door around its settling), all wrapped by the one `StepError` constructor against an execution cursor.
rows.note: D-223 put a catch in boundary zero. D-441 (log.md:18439) rules that every catch site wraps what reaches it and names the restore door's catch. There is one constructor but no longer one catch site.

rows.claim: D-088: `init!`'s absence is a diagnostic distinct from `UninitializedSlots`.
rows.evidence: No `UninitializedSlots` exists. The kind is `UninitializedInputs` (src/diagnostics.jl:2080). The absence of `init!` is `MissingInit` (src/diagnostics.jl:1266, src/sim.jl:604-605).
rows.note: Stage M lead (names missing: UninitializedSlots). Renamed by D-206 (log.md:8257, 8269). The annotation at log.md:3028 records it.

rows.claim: D-097: the `DeviceCrash` payload carries the device id.
rows.evidence: `struct DeviceCrash` has only the fields `cause` and `abort` (src/diagnostics.jl:1688-1691; probe:87 prints (:cause, :abort)). Writer attribution is never a payload field. The cell supplies it (src/diagnostics.jl:1563-1564).
rows.fix: `DeviceCrash` (exception as `cause`, the `should_abort` disposition as `abort`; the device is attributed by its diagnostic cell)
rows.note: Moved by D-228 (log.md:9316): runtime diagnostics are attributed by cell, never by payload. `DeviceJoinTimeout`'s `who` stays, because it names the subject (Appendix C).

rows.claim: D-110: resume-at-time is spelled by passing `capture`'s returned `t` as `trim!`'s `t0`.
rows.evidence: `capture` is not defined in Redstone (probe:95 prints false). A state past t0 is a `Checkpoint` (src/checkpoint.jl:106-110), resumed by `restore!` (src/sim.jl:1063), which inherits the clock.
rows.fix: resume-at-time spelled explicitly by passing the time as `t0`; `capture` is retired (D-273), and a resume proper is `checkpoint` then `restore!`
rows.note: Stage M lead (names missing: capture at 3807). D-273 (log.md:12241) retired `capture`'s condition form, and D-274 made the checkpoint the resume value.

rows.claim: D-198: D-133's other three fixed operational constants stand, `margin` = 2 ms with no user knob among them.
rows.evidence: `margin` is a user knob. `run!` and `replay!` take `margin = 0.002` (src/sim.jl:1562, 1335), `margin!(sim, m)` writes it (src/sim.jl:2412), and the wait reads it off the control plane (src/control.jl:185). The other two stay fixed: debt forgiveness `5*h/p` (src/control.jl:177) and staleness 2 s (src/dataplane.jl:309).
rows.fix: This amends D-133: its semantic/operational split stands, and so do its debt bound `5·h/p` and its 2 s staleness; `margin`, 2 ms by default, became a knob under D-269.
rows.note: Moved by D-269 (log.md:11891), which made `margin` a knob with `margin!` and the `run!`/`replay!` keyword.

rows.claim: D-223: a throw inside boundary zero can occur under `replay!`, wrapped with host boundary zero's rule.
rows.evidence: `replay!` runs no boundary zero. It restores the header through `_enter_checkpoint!` (src/sim.jl:995-1003, 1396-1398), and `init!` is the one door that runs boundary zero (src/model.jl:699-700). A throw in `replay!`'s restore arrives with host :restore and the state's frame as pointer (src/model.jl:1331-1341).
rows.fix: A throw inside boundary zero, under `init!`, is wrapped by the one `StepError` constructor ...; a throw inside `replay!`'s restore takes the restore door's catch, host `:restore`.
rows.note: Moved by D-274 (log.md:12360-12365: replay restores the header, and `init!` is the only door that runs boundary zero) and D-441 (the restore door's own catch).

rows.claim: D-223: `replay!` of the captured header reproduces either failure at pointer zero.
rows.evidence: A boundary-zero throw leaves no header and no trace. The header is written only after `init!`'s boundary zero returns (src/sim.jl:852-856), and `trace(sim)` is refused as `MissingInit` afterwards (probe:77). The reproduction is `init!` under the same condition (src/diagnostics.jl:320-321).
rows.fix: `init!` under the same condition reproduces a boundary-zero failure, and `replay!` of the header then `step!` reproduces frame one's.
rows.note: Moved by D-274's last bullet (log.md:12378-12387): a throw inside boundary zero leaves no trace and no checkpoint, and its reproduction is `init!` under the same condition.

rows.claim: D-223: the rendered recipe at pointer zero is the bare replay.
rows.evidence: `showerror` renders "init!(sim2, condition) under the same condition reproduces it" for host :boundary_zero (probe:78) and "replay!(sim2, trc; to_boundary = 0) then step!(sim2) reproduces it" for frame one (probe:84), per src/diagnostics.jl:296-327. Neither is a bare replay.
rows.fix: the rendered recipe at zero follows the host: `init!` under the same condition for boundary zero, and the halt then `step!` for frame one
rows.note: Moved by D-274 (log.md:12378-12387, amended 2026-09-30). The general recipe holds from pointer 0 for a frame's failure.

rows.claim: D-223: an interrupt inside boundary zero propagates raw.
rows.evidence: The boundary-zero catch wraps every throw (src/model.jl:335-339). test/test_failures.jl:473-475 asserts `StepError{InterruptException}` with host :boundary_zero and lifecycle :built. The `init!` docstring at src/sim.jl:815-816 says the same.
rows.fix: An interrupt inside boundary zero moves the lifecycle to `built` and arrives wrapped in a `StepError` with host `:boundary_zero`; a service has no stop path.
rows.note: Moved by D-441 (log.md:18439-18441): every catch site wraps what reaches it, an `InterruptException` included. The first half of the bullet (lifecycle to built) still holds.

rows.claim: D-389: the §12.2 liveness heartbeat is run-scoped.
rows.evidence: The heartbeat lives in the device's `DiagCell` and is never reset after `attach!` (src/dataplane.jl:124-130). `stale(record)` judges any record against the wall clock, with no run scoping (src/dataplane.jl:337-338). Stopped-time publications from `init!`/`restore!` carry it too (src/sim.jl:2835). `orphaned` is run-scoped through `task_state` :none outside a run (src/sim.jl:2831).
rows.note: Whether "run-scoped" is a semantic statement (liveness means nothing while stopped, as D-089 at log.md:3142-3169 frames it) or a rule the code must enforce cannot be settled from the code. Nothing scopes `stale` or resets the heartbeat per run.

rows.claim: D-398: Julia's forced throw after repeated SIGINTs ends `stopped` with the frame abandoned, stores possibly mid-boundary until the next door.
rows.evidence: `frame!`'s catch wraps every throw inside the frame, the forced interrupt included, and writes :inconsistent (src/frame.jl:94-97). The loop arm rethrows the `StepError` (src/sim.jl:2123-2139), and the run records `LoopError` and reads `errored` (src/sim.jl:1751-1762, 515). `init!`, `replay!` and `restore!` all refuse `errored` (src/sim.jl:839, 1344).
rows.fix: Julia's forced throw after repeated SIGINTs lands inside the frame, is wrapped by `frame!`'s catch, and ends the run `errored` under `LoopError`.
rows.note: D-441 (log.md:18447-18449) supersedes this bullet explicitly, and D-441 is ratified, so the chain ends at a ratified entry. D-398's Status still reads plainly ratified with no partial-supersession mark.
